A cell begins as a vector of molecular counts / 03 / Cell / CD3D / MS4A1 / NKG7 / Total UMIs / A / 4 / 0 / 1 / 1,000 / B / 8 / 0 / 2 / 2,000 / C / 0 / 6 / 0 / 1,200 / Each gene supplies one coordinate / Zero means no detected molecule / The full matrix contains many more genes / Illustrative counts. Total UMIs include genes omitted from this table. / Each UMI is intended to identify one captured mRNA molecule, rather than every mRNA molecule present in the cell.

QC changes which cells enter the geometry / Luecken & Theis 2019, Figure 2, CC BY 4.0 / 04 / Count depth and detected genes / Mitochondrial fraction in context / Thresholds depend on tissue and sample

Normalization changes the meaning of a distance / 05 / Cell / Gene count / Total UMIs / Per 10,000 / log1p / A / 4 / 1,000 / 40 / 3.714 / B / 8 / 2,000 / 40 / 3.714 / yᵢⱼ = log(1 + 10,000 × cᵢⱼ / totalᵢ) / Library-size normalization reduces depth differences / log1p compresses the expression range / Illustrative arithmetic. Equal normalized values do not establish equal absolute RNA content.

HVG selection and scaling define the gene space / 06 / Operation / What changes / What stays meaningful / HVG selection / Columns used for geometry / Original counts remain available / Centering / Gene mean becomes zero / Relative position of cells / Unit-variance scaling / Each gene has variance one / Gene-wise standardized deviations / HVGs emphasize variation beyond the mean–variance trend / Scaling is a modeling choice, not a universal requirement / Classic log-normalized workflow. HVG methods differ in expected input.

Batch correction changes local relationships / Luecken & Theis 2019, Figure 3, CC BY 4.0 / 07 / Before and after correction / Mixing alone does not validate integration / Biology can be confounded with batch

Many genes share fewer patterns of variation / 08 / Co-regulated genes contribute redundant information / Technical variation adds unwanted directions / A compact representation can improve neighbor search / 20,000 genes     2,000 HVGs     30 PCs     2 UMAP coordinates / Illustrative dimensions, not recommended fixed settings
PCA rotates the axes, truncation removes directions / 09 / PC1 captures the largest remaining variance. PC2 is orthogonal to PC1.

Loadings describe genes, scores locate cells / 10 / T = ZVₖ / Z: centered expression for the selected genes / Vₖ: gene weights for each retained component / T: one row per cell, one column per PC / PC1 score = 0.6 × Gene A + 0.8 × Gene B / Illustrative loading vector. Genes A and B denote centered, optionally scaled expression.

Truncating PCA changes the distances between cells / 11 / d²(i,j) = Σₗ₌₁ᵏ (Tᵢₗ − Tⱼₗ)² / The retained PCs define the comparison space / All PCs preserve centered Euclidean geometry / Discarded PCs no longer contribute to distance / For an orthonormal PCA basis, without whitening

The elbow is a starting point for choosing PCs / Luecken & Theis 2019, Figure 4F, CC BY 4.0 / 12 / This dataset has an elbow around PCs 5–7 / Inspect loadings and QC associations / Check whether neighborhoods remain stable

A strong PC can reflect sequencing depth / Luecken & Theis 2019, Figure 4A, CC BY 4.0 / 13 / Cells share the count-depth color scale in Figure 4 / PCA optimizes variance without biological labels / Depth associations require investigation

Neighbor search defines local cell relationships / 14 / Candidate / PC coordinates / Distance from A / Among 2 nearest? / A / (0, 0, 0) / 0 / Reference / B / (0.1, 0.2, 0.1) / 0.245 / Yes / C / (2, 0, 0) / 2 / Yes / D / (0, 3, 0) / 3 / No / Each cell searches in the retained PC space / A graph records local connectivity and weights / Toy example with Euclidean distance and k = 2. A is excluded from its own candidates.

UMAP fits a layout to a weighted graph / 15 / Local distances define connection strengths / Nearby cells attract in the embedding objective / Repulsion helps separate weakly connected cells / Optimization trades off conflicting relationships / The output gives each cell two display coordinates / Conceptual summary of UMAP’s fuzzy graph objective and negative-sampling optimization
The same cells produce different views of structure / Luecken & Theis 2019, Figure 4, CC BY 4.0 / 16

min_dist changes how tightly points pack / Official UMAP tutorial, synthetic data / 17 / Same synthetic color dataset from the official UMAP tutorial / Smaller min_dist allows tighter packing / n_neighbors controls the neighborhood scale

PCA and UMAP solve different problems / 18 / Property / PCA used for representation / UMAP used for display / Objective / Capture variance in orthogonal axes / Approximate weighted local relationships / Typical output here / Several dozen coordinates / Two coordinates / Interpretation / Gene loadings and cell scores / Relative layout and local neighborhoods / Main limitation / Linear axes may miss nonlinear structure / Global distances and density can distort / UMAP can run without PCA and can output more than two dimensions.

Clustering and UMAP use related representations / 19 / Task / Usual input / Result / Neighbor construction / Retained PCs or integrated latent space / Weighted cell relationships / Clustering / A neighborhood graph, often with SNN weighting / A discrete label per cell / UMAP visualization / PC-derived neighborhoods or a supplied graph / Two display coordinates / Cluster labels usually appear as colors on UMAP / Changing layout settings need not change the clusters

UMAP distances need evidence beyond the picture / 20 / Nearby cells suggest local similarity worth checking / A gap does not prove a discrete cell type / Island area does not estimate population abundance / An apparent path does not establish lineage or time / Would the conclusion survive a different reasonable representation?

Different analysis tasks use different data layers / Luecken & Theis 2019, Table 1, teaching summary, CC BY 4.0 / 21 / Task / Appropriate representation / Library-aware count models and pseudobulk / Retained raw counts with sample metadata / Gene-expression display / An appropriate normalized gene-expression layer / Neighbor search and graph clustering / Selected PC scores or a suitable latent space / Visual exploration / UMAP coordinates, colored by independent metadata / Teaching summary based on Table 1. Statistical input depends on the chosen method.

The full chain explains the final map / 22 / Counts record sampled molecules / QC and normalization define comparable observations / HVGs and scaling define the gene space / PCA and neighbor search define local similarity / UMAP supplies the display coordinates / Every visible island inherits upstream decisions

Discussion: which decision changes the conclusion? / 23 / A rare population disappears when we use fewer PCs / A cluster becomes tighter after changing min_dist / Samples mix after integration, but a disease state disappears / Which result needs a representation check, a layout check, or biological validation?

The classical Seurat sequence / 32 / Appendix / obj <- NormalizeData(obj) / obj <- FindVariableFeatures(obj, nfeatures = 2000) / obj <- ScaleData(obj, features = VariableFeatures(obj)) / obj <- RunPCA(obj, features = VariableFeatures(obj)) / obj <- FindNeighbors(obj, dims = 1:30) / obj <- FindClusters(obj, resolution = 0.5) / obj <- RunUMAP(obj, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:30) / Assumes QC is complete. Illustrative settings, not optimized defaults. SCTransform follows an alternative route.

The classical Scanpy sequence / 33 / Appendix / adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy() / sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4) / sc.pp.log1p(adata) / sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, flavor="seurat", /                           n_top_genes=2000) / sc.pp.scale(adata, max_value=10) / sc.pp.pca(adata, n_comps=50, mask_var="highly_variable") / sc.pp.neighbors(adata, n_pcs=30, n_neighbors=15) / sc.tl.umap(adata, random_state=0) / sc.tl.leiden(adata, resolution=0.5) / Assumes QC is complete and X initially contains counts. Illustrative settings. Scaling can increase memory use.
